rationale: D7 CLAIMED — ISO-C CITATION emission (task-21 follow-up). The Lead landed the citation mechanism as the existing namespace claim kind (`metadata.languageNamespace`); the C lane emits it for the `iso-c-stdlib-name` class with roots copied as a SUBSET of the committed vocabulary `ISO_C_STDLIB` (id "iso-c-stdlib", script/m14/citations.ts, source ISO/IEC 9899). A C standard-library name is a BARE symbol, so the claim cites exactly its target (`languageNamespace: [target]`) — a valid subset, reviewable on the edge. Emission is gated on the analyzer's existing condition that the target is NOT declared in the file, so a project-declared name can never be excused by the claim. BOTH DIRECTIONS PINNED: three positives (`strlen`, `malloc`, `memcpy` — listed, undeclared here) MUST carry the exact citation; three negatives MUST stay uncited — (a) `free`, LISTED but DECLARED in this file (the claim may never excuse a project name), (b) `strlcpy`, a BSD library name NOT in the ISO-C vocabulary (the vocabulary is the authority; a lane may not invent names into a citation), (c) `PyObject_Call`, a third-party name outside the vocabulary. The call edges themselves are unchanged — the claim is metadata on the same edge, and the arbiter treats a namespace claim as its sole authority (incoming-rule.ts `classifyEdge`), which is why the negatives are load-bearing: an over-broad emission here would convert project-declared and unlisted rows into verified-external claims. Evidence probe: script/m14/c-citation-probe.ts (contract PASSED on this fixture; prints each row's citation).
